et: borrowed from Middle French {it}roquete,{/it} borrowed from Italian (15th-century) {it}ruchetta, rochetta,{/it} from {it}ruca{/it} "arugula" (going back to Latin {it}ērūca{/it} "arugula, caterpillar," of uncertain origin) + {it}-etta,{/it} diminutive suffix, going back to Latin {it}-itta{/it}

The sense "caterpillar" of Latin {it}ērūca{/it} has been taken as the original one, with the plant so called from the resemblance of its hairy stems to a caterpillar. If this is the case, {it}ērūca{/it} could be a derivative of {it}*ēr{/it} "hedgehog" (see {et_link|urchin|urchin}); the suffix may be the same as in {it}festūca{/it} "stalk, straw," {it}lactūca{/it} "lettuce," and {it}verrūca{/it} "wart."
shortdef: any of several plants of the mustard family: such as
